title: Four Signs You’re a Mentally Weak Man
author: Michael Clary
summary: Pastor Michael Clary adapts a talk to the men of his church into an argument that mental toughness is a basic part of faithful manhood, not a pastoral extra. Drawing on Proverbs, he names four warning signs of weakness: being easily offended, being unable to control anger, being unable to take criticism, and failing to push through adversity. For each he offers a practical correction, such as deliberately overlooking minor slights, restraining anger and then channeling it into focus, inviting a trusted friend to name blind spots, and getting back up after being knocked down. He is explicit that toughness does not mean being cold or emotionless; it means not letting emotions rule one's life. He tells his own story of thin-skinned early ministry and a season of severe stress as evidence that these habits can be learned by discipline and trial. The piece closes with four concrete commitments to begin that week.
points: Clary defines toughness as emotional governance rather than coldness: a mentally strong man feels the full range of emotions but does not let them run his life.
Taking offense is framed as a choice, and "overlooking an offense" is treated as a deliberate act that most slights, born of bruised ego, deserve.
Anger is neither suppressed nor vented; the strong man restrains it and then lets it sharpen his focus, where the weak man becomes more impulsive.
He proposes a concrete exercise, asking a trusted friend to name two or three growth areas "brutally honestly," which tests the friendship and exposes blind spots.
Weakness does not disappear on its own, so he ends with four disciplines to practice immediately: overlook, restrain, listen without defending, and get back up.
quotes: Mental toughness doesn’t mean being cold, stoic, or emotionless. We’re humans, not robots, and God made us capable of feeling a broad range of emotions.
Being mentally tough is about not letting your emotions rule your life, especially when you feel like giving up. A mentally tough man doesn’t fall apart when life hits him hard.
Some people tend to their grievances like the curator of a museum. Ancient insults are kept behind glass, brightly lit for all to see.
Our culture incentivizes this. We train people to be irresponsible and emotionally immature by rewarding those who are easily offended. Grievance has become a form of currency.
The mentally weak man gets angry and becomes more impulsive. The mentally strong man gets angry and becomes more focused.
The scoffer protects his ego, but the wise man protects his character. To become strong and wise, you have to be the kind of man people feel safe correcting.
You’re gonna get knocked down, everyone does. But do you get back up and keep going after that?
Weakness doesn't disappear on its own; we have to discipline it out of ourselves.
